explanation: Emit 2 separately and store flags only for odd candidates 2i+3. For each unmarked candidate p, emit p and mark its odd multiples beginning at p²; in compressed indices these advance by p.
timeComplexity: O(n log log n) for n≥3: initialization and the candidate scan cost O(n), while marking over primes costs O(n Σ(1/p)) = O(n log log n). Smaller inputs take constant time.
spaceComplexity: O(n) including about n/2 flags for odd candidates and the returned primes. Compressing odd candidates improves the constant, not the asymptotic bound.

correctness: Every composite integer has a prime factor no larger than its square root. Before a candidate p is reached, every composite with a smaller prime factor has therefore been marked; an unmarked p is prime. Multiples below p² have a smaller prime factor and need no new marking. Marking from p² excludes every remaining composite divisible by p. All even numbers except 2 are composite, so omitting their flags loses no prime. Index i represents 2i+3; increasing the index by p increases the candidate by 2p, visiting exactly the odd multiples.
walkthrough: For n=12, emit 2. The flags represent 3,5,7,9,11. Candidate 3 is unmarked, so emit it and mark 9, its first composite odd multiple. Candidates 5,7 and 11 remain unmarked and are emitted; their squares exceed 12. Return [2,3,5,7,11].
edgeCases: The upper bound is inclusive: n=2 returns [2].
Begin marking at p², not p, or a prime would eliminate itself.
